channel.title: AgentSee Podcast
channel.description: James Hartt and Abrar Mahmood are building a software agency from the ground up, in public, with agents doing the work. Every agency was organised around one scarce thing, engineering time, and that constraint has moved. Each episode is what they actually did, what it cost, what broke, and which of their stated questions it touched.
channel.itunes:author: AgentSee

item.title: Introductions and the premise
item.itunes:title: Introductions and the premise
item.description:
James Hartt and Abrar Mahmood introduce themselves and the premise of AgentSee: a software agency for a world where working software can be prompted into existence. Agencies were organised around protecting developer time and billing for it; when that is no longer the expensive part, what does a client pay for? Their answer, for now, is the last stretch to production, which is as hard as it ever was.

Chapters:

  • 00:00 Welcome, and who we are
  • 02:32 The premise: what agencies were built to protect
  • 04:43 What a client pays for now
  • 05:49 Where the value is: the last five percent
  • 07:34 Wrap up
  • 07:59 Outro

Mentioned:

  • Issue No. 1: the premise, and the ten questions

Of the questions on the site, this one touches:

  • 1. If writing the code is no longer the expensive part, what is the client actually buying?
  • 7. What does taste mean when volume is free?

AgentSee is two people building a company in public, with agents doing the work.

https://agentsee.work · hello@agentsee.work

Subscribe: https://agentsee.work/podcast/feed.xml
